marks.gloss_en: דגמירי דמיהב יהבי מישקל לא שקלי
he: are you content that everyone will eat at a complete table and we at a defective one? she: pray that it be taken from you; he prayed and they took it
תניא, פלימו אומר: אני ראיתי אותו הבית והיו קורותיו יוצאות אמה לכאן ואמה לכאן -- kind svara: no support kind names a bare תניא
a tanna taught: they reached until they protruded a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side
שהרי אדם גדול הטיח דברים כלפי מעלה ואיטלע, ומנו -- לוי
Levi decreed a fast and no rain came; he said: Master of the world, You went up and sat on high and do not have mercy on Your children; rain came, and he became lame
ורבי חנינא בן דוסא מהיכן הוו ליה עזים? והא עני הוי! -- he was poor (a kav of carobs from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve)
R' Pinchas's maaseh: the goats were bought with the proceeds of chickens a man had left at his door (= p_pinchas_tarnegolin)
ועוד, אמרו חכמים: אין מגדלין בהמה דקה בארץ ישראל -- how could he keep goats? (kind tanya for the formula אמרו חכמים; see header)
and the Sages said: one does not raise small cattle in the Land of Israel
the same maaseh: the goats belonged to the man who lost the chickens, and were returned to him; the text gives one answer to the double question and does not spell out how it meets this prong

R' Pinchas: a man passed his door and left chickens there; R' Chanina's wife found them, and he told her: do not eat their eggs; they multiplied and distressed them, so he sold them and bought goats with the proceeds; when the man came back and gave a sign, he took the goats -- and these are the goats that brought bears on their horns
הא גרמא ליה? והא לוי אחוי קידה קמיה דרבי ואיטלע! -- his lameness came from the kidda he demonstrated before Rebbi
הא והא גרמא ליה -- both caused it
but Levi demonstrated kidda [bowing] before Rebbi and became lame
she had a bad neighbour, who said: I know they have nothing at all -- what is all this? she went and knocked on the door; [the wife] was embarrassed and went into an inner room
a miracle was done for her: [the neighbour] saw the oven full of bread and the trough full of dough, and called: so-and-so, bring a peel, your bread is burning! she said: I too went in for that
at his wife's urging (until when shall we suffer so?) he prayed, and something like the palm of a hand came out and gave him one leg of a golden table

one Shabbat eve he saw his daughter sad -- she had lit the Shabbat lamp from vinegar mistaken for oil; he said: my daughter, why does it matter to you? He who told the oil to burn will tell the vinegar to burn
R' Chanina ben Dosa had some goats
to a neighbour whose house-beams did not reach: what is your name? Eichu. He said: Eichu, may your beams reach

R' Elazar ben Pedat was in great poverty; after bloodletting he had nothing to eat but a clove of garlic, fainted and slept; the Sages visiting saw him weeping and laughing, and a ray of fire coming from his forehead
R' Elazar: the Holy One was sitting with me, and I said to Him: until when shall I suffer in this world?
R' Elazar: all this, and only 'perhaps'? is what remains greater than what I have lived? -- what you have lived; I said: if so, I do not want it
the Holy One: as reward for saying 'I do not want it', I will give you in the world to come thirteen rivers of pure balsam oil, like the Euphrates and the Tigris, to delight in
R' Chama bar Chanina decreed a fast and no rain came; told that R' Yehoshua ben Levi decreed one and rain came, he said: this is I, and that is the son of Levi
after a further prayer failed: would you like rain to come for our sake? yes. He said: sky, sky, cover your face! it did not; he said: how brazen is the face of the sky! it covered over and rain came

R' Chiyya bar Luliani heard the clouds say: let us go pour water in Ammon and Moab; he said: Master of the world, when You gave the Torah You offered it to all the nations and they did not accept it, and now You give them rain? pour here! they poured it in their place
